name: document-templates
description: Invoices and other documents from templates, fully local: a ready-made invoice or your own layout to PDF, fillable PDF forms and Word templates filled in, saved in tidy folders with running numbers

nodes.title: List templates
nodes.description: Lists the ready-made templates and the kinds of template you can bring yourself (your own layout, a PDF form, a Word document), with the operation for each

outputs.name: next_cursor
outputs.description: Cursor for the next page, empty when there is none

nodes.title: Describe a template
nodes.description: Shows what a template needs before you fill it: for the invoice or your own layout, its fields with an example; for a Word document, its {{placeholders}}; for a PDF form, its boxes (or that it has none)

template.description: `invoice` (the ready-made template), or a .json, .docx, .dotx or .pdf file in your templates folder

include_layout.description: For the invoice or your own layout: also return the whole design. To get a copy you can change, use save_template_copy instead

outputs.name: next_cursor
outputs.description: Cursor for the next page, empty when there is none

nodes.title: Save a copy of a template to change
nodes.description: Saves your own copy of a ready-made template in your documents folder (in the folder Templates), so that you can change its texts, colours and layout while the original stays as it is. Nothing is ever replaced: when the name is taken, the copy gets a number. To use your copy, give its `path` as `template` when creating a PDF

name.description: A name for your copy, without extension, e.g. "Quotation" (default: the template's own name)

outputs.name: next_cursor
outputs.description: Cursor for the next page, empty when there is none

nodes.title: Next document number
nodes.description: Gives the next number of a series, such as INV-2026-0001, then INV-2026-0002, so that no two documents get the same number. The count starts again with each new year (or month, when the pattern has one). The last number is remembered in your documents folder

pattern.description: Number pattern with one {SEQ} (or {SEQ:4} for four digits) and optional {YYYY} {YY} {MM} {DD} {ROMAN} (month as a Roman numeral), e.g. "{SEQ:3}/INV/{ROMAN}/{YYYY}"

date.description: Date the number is for, as YYYY-MM-DD (default: today)

start_at.description: First number of a counter that has not been used yet, e.g. 38 to continue after INV-2026-0037

preview.description: Only show what the next number would be, without using it up

outputs.name: next_cursor
outputs.description: Cursor for the next page, empty when there is none

nodes.title: Create a PDF from a template
nodes.description: Creates a PDF document, such as an invoice, from a template and your values: the ready-made `invoice`, or your own template. Totals are calculated for you and a long list of items continues on the next page. The PDF is saved in your documents folder, sorted by year and month (2026/11/INV-2026-0001.pdf), and a document that is already there is never replaced. The result says where the file is

template.description: `invoice` (the ready-made template), or your own template: a .json file in your templates folder, or the `path` that save_template_copy returned

values.description: The document's values as an object (or JSON text), e.g. {"number": "INV-2026-0001", "client": {"name": "PT Maju"}, "items": [...]}. describe_template lists what a template uses

values_file.description: Instead of `values`: a .json file with the values, in your templates folder

calculate.description: invoice: calculate line amounts, subtotal, discount, taxes and totals from `items` (exact decimals) and add them as `totals`; none: use the values as given; auto (default): a layout template decides (the built-in invoice calculates), a Word or PDF form template calculates when the values have `items`

background.description: A PDF in your templates folder that is drawn under every page, e.g. your letterhead (its page 1 under the first page, its page 2, if any, under the others)

folder.description: Leave this empty unless a particular folder was asked for: documents are then sorted by year and month (2026/11) inside your documents folder. To sort them another way, write a pattern such as "Invoices/{client}/{YYYY}". Tokens: {YYYY} {MM} {DD} (the document's date, else today), {number}, {client}, {template} and {values.some.field}

file_name.description: Leave this empty to name the file after the document's number (INV-2026-0001). Or a name without extension, as a pattern with the same tokens as `folder`, e.g. "{number} {client}"

if_exists.description: What to do when a document with this name is already there: error (keep it and report the problem; the default), number (keep both: the new one is saved as name-2, name-3, ...) or overwrite (replace it; only a step of a saved agent may do this, never a request made in chat)

outputs.name: next_cursor
outputs.description: Cursor for the next page, empty when there is none

nodes.title: Fill in a PDF form
nodes.description: Fills in a PDF form (a PDF with boxes you can type in) and saves the result as a new PDF in your documents folder. `fields` says which value goes into which box; a value may use {{placeholders}} from `values`, including calculated totals such as {{totals.total | money}}. A PDF without such boxes (a scan, a picture, plain pages) cannot be filled in: use render_pdf

template.description: The PDF form, a .pdf file in your templates folder

fields.description: Form field names and their values, e.g. {"InvoiceNo": "{{number}}", "Total": "{{totals.total | money}}", "Paid": true}

fields_file.description: Instead of `fields`: a .json file with the field names and values, in your templates folder (reusable for every document from this form)

values.description: The document's values as an object (or JSON text), e.g. {"number": "INV-2026-0001", "client": {"name": "PT Maju"}, "items": [...]}. describe_template lists what a template uses

values_file.description: Instead of `values`: a .json file with the values, in your templates folder

calculate.description: invoice: calculate line amounts, subtotal, discount, taxes and totals from `items` (exact decimals) and add them as `totals`; none: use the values as given; auto (default): a layout template decides (the built-in invoice calculates), a Word or PDF form template calculates when the values have `items`

flatten.description: Make the filled-in values a fixed part of the page, so that nobody can change them afterwards (default true)

folder.description: Leave this empty unless a particular folder was asked for: documents are then sorted by year and month (2026/11) inside your documents folder. To sort them another way, write a pattern such as "Invoices/{client}/{YYYY}". Tokens: {YYYY} {MM} {DD} (the document's date, else today), {number}, {client}, {template} and {values.some.field}

file_name.description: Leave this empty to name the file after the document's number (INV-2026-0001). Or a name without extension, as a pattern with the same tokens as `folder`, e.g. "{number} {client}"

if_exists.description: What to do when a document with this name is already there: error (keep it and report the problem; the default), number (keep both: the new one is saved as name-2, name-3, ...) or overwrite (replace it; only a step of a saved agent may do this, never a request made in chat)

outputs.name: next_cursor
outputs.description: Cursor for the next page, empty when there is none

nodes.title: Fill in a Word template
nodes.description: Fills in a Word document that has {{placeholders}} (.docx, or a Word template .dotx) and saves the result as a new Word file in your documents folder. A table row between {{#items}} and {{/items}} repeats for every item, and totals are calculated for you. The result is a Word file, not a PDF

values.description: The document's values as an object (or JSON text), e.g. {"number": "INV-2026-0001", "client": {"name": "PT Maju"}, "items": [...]}. describe_template lists what a template uses

file_name.description: Leave this empty to name the file after the document's number (INV-2026-0001). Or a name without extension, as a pattern with the same tokens as `folder`, e.g. "{number} {client}"
